newsitem.title: MEXICO: President of Mexico's ruling PRI resigns.
newsitem.headline: President of Mexico's ruling PRI resigns.

text.p: The president of Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party resigned on Friday in the latest sign of a political crisis in the party that has ruled Mexico for 67 years.

In his letter of resignation, Santiago Onate Labourde, who headed the party of President Ernesto Zedillo for the last 16 months, said the party needed a determined thrust in order to win key mid-term elections set for next year.

"I am confident that the decision that I have taken will allow me to contribute with greater efficiency from other trenches to the ongoing battle in a common cause for democracy and social justice," Onate said.
He added that the time and circumstances were right for a change of leadership before mid-term elections in Mexico next year.
Government news agency Notimex said that the national executive committee of the party is expected to chose a new leader on Sunday.

The party has suffered a number of setbacks recently, with the latest being a series of defections of party members this week. More seriously, the PRI suffered reversals in state elections in November, and faces a number of hotly contested local elections across Mexico in mid-1997.
Onate, who held various positions within the party and was a former Minister of Labour, said that the shake-up of the PRI leadership will help the party win the upcoming elections.

Next year there will be seven races for governor, 271 Congressional seats on the line, and elections for 264 municipal presidents. The mayor of Mexico City will be determined in an election for the first time.

On Wednesday, Virginia Betanzos, a legislator from the southeastern state of Quintana Roo, announced her resignation from the PRI, claiming that PRI dissidents in her state had been beaten up by party thugs who enjoyed legal impunity.

Betanzos was the third legislator to quit the PRI in the past three weeks in protest at the growing influence of party "dinosaurs" -- hardliners who want to turn back the clock on reforms and preserve the party's decades-old grip on power.
Early on Friday party deputies and senators told reporters that a change was needed in the post of president of the party after the losses the party suffered in the recent elections.
Television news reports said a powerful PRI deputy in the lower house, Humberto Roque Villanueva, is set to take over from Onate.
